headline: A Moderna co-founder has called for urgent regulation of AI agents, warning that waiting for a disaster would repeat mistakes the drug industry made.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a clear call confirmed by the report's opening paragraphs, but no proposals or setting are known because the rest was paywalled.
importance_line: A prominent drug-industry founder asking for rules before harm occurs adds pressure on sellers of AI agents, which matters first to the people who will use these tools, then to regulators, then to the companies, but his proposals and the place and time of his remarks are not known.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Noubar Afeyan, co-founder of the biotech company Moderna, has called for urgent regulation of AI agents (software that carries out tasks for a user) that technology firms are selling, comparing the risk of waiting for a disaster to the thalidomide tragedy of the 1950s and 60s, when a drug taken by pregnant women caused birth defects, and arguing that companies profiting from AI agents must take responsibility for their safety before launch.
notes: Bloomberg's page showed only its opening paragraphs (paywall), so verified_text is false; no other outlet's text could be opened (Quartz and Crypto Briefing blocked).
